0.90 — UI documents declare host slots, and synthesis witnesses guards over lists of identities | ESS0.90.0 lets an ess-ui/1 document declare host slots, the places the host application draws with its own component, and checks them. Conformance synthesis witnesses a guard over a list of identities beside an updates subject, in a creating command and over several literals, and a null entry of a tags field draws no chip.ESSfield-noteessfield-noteadopterdevelopertry-spec-driven-developmentresearch

Source-owned field note · website/blog/2026-11-07-1200-host-slots-and-list-guard-witnesses.md · revision 5c54de2902f8

0.90.0 changes the ess-ui/1 document and its checker, conformance synthesis and the tags field of the React and terminal renderers. No source format moves, and ess-ui/1 stays /1: a host slot is an optional node, so a document without one loads, checks and renders as before. The synthesis fixes close the gaps #761 describes. The changelog lists every change.

Before you upgrade​

  • An ess before 0.90.0 refuses a document that declares a host slot, naming host as an unknown key.
  • ess generate ui --target react and the terminal renderer refuse a document holding a host slot, naming its path, until host slots are generated in 0.91.0. Declare slots now to check them; generate from such a document once 0.91.0 is out.

Host slots​

  • A node carrying host is a host slot: a place the host application draws with its own component and ESS does not draw. It names the component the host registers (host), why the generator cannot draw it (reason), what it stands in for (stands_in_for), and optionally the view and commands the component uses (reads, commands).
  • A slot stands at a page, a section, an overlay, a tab or a field; its node path is its scope.
  • ess ui check refuses a slot without a reason or without stands_in_for, two slots of one host name, and a slot beside component or primitive. With --hosts <file> it refuses a registered name no slot declares.
  • stands_in_for is a composite, a primitive or none. The slots standing in for none are listed as the generator's backlog, in the text report and in the ess-ui-check/1 JSON report.

Guards over lists of identities​

  • A refusal over a list of identities beside a branch acting on a row the input names is sent for a row that branch arranges, so the not-found answer no longer decides its scenario first.
  • A branch whose own guard the empty list refutes is sent the list its witness holds, each element a row created under it. Where that branch is the only route to a row, it is sent a list that satisfies the guard instead of being refused.
  • A guard that needs several literals in one list, all: [exists a: …, exists b: …], is witnessed by one list holding every literal; before, it was refused ESS-SYNTH-003.
  • Known limit: the negated side of such a guard, not exists b: …, is not yet tested, so a target that ignores the negation passes the suite. A story tracks it.

Tags fields​

  • A null entry of an as: tags field draws no chip in the React target or the terminal, and the tags input neither shows, compares nor writes back a held null.

items.content_html:
0.89 — A route takes a bare body, a literal segment wins, and an each write takes repeated identities | ESS0.89.0 lets a command route take one input field as its whole request body, lets a literal path segment take precedence over a variable one, adds format ess/35, in which an each write may name one row more than once, and stamps each generated file with its own slice's digest only. UI documents gain a contains search, tag suggestions, toggle checks and a header help node.ESSfield-noteessfield-noteadopterdevelopertry-spec-driven-developmentresearch

Source-owned field note · website/blog/2026-11-06-2200-bare-bodies-literal-routes-and-repeated-identities.md · revision 5c54de2902f8

0.89.0 adds one source format, ess/35, and moves the generated-output checkpoint to ess-output-state/4, which releases before 0.89.0 refuse. The HTTP and specification changes come from a downstream specification's report (#748). A model that uses none of the new spellings keeps its IR bytes. The changelog lists every change.

Before you upgrade​

  • ess generate writes .ess-output/state.json as ess-output-state/4. An ess older than 0.89.0 refuses that checkpoint, so every ess that generates into or checks such a root must be 0.89.0 or later. 0.89.0 still reads /1 to /3.
  • A generated file no longer carries the model digest line, and the JSON Schema, OpenAPI and AsyncAPI documents no longer carry source_digest. A file committed by an earlier release is reported by ess generate --check as differing until the root is generated again.

HTTP bindings​

  • A command route may take one input field as its whole request body, request: {encoding: json, body: input.<field>}, with every other input field in the path. OpenAPI publishes the field's own schema as the body, the generated Rust and Go servers read the body as that field, and the React and terminal renderers send the field's value alone.
  • Two nested route templates of one component and method are admitted when one holds the literal at every segment where they differ, and the more specific answers: /boards/{board_id}/cards/priority beside /boards/{board_id}/cards/{card_id}. Crossed templates stay refused, and the refusal names a path both match.

Repeated identities in list order​

  • From ess/35 an affects: entry over an input list may take a list naming one row more than once, each: {in: input.<list>, as: <name>, repeated: last_wins}, with no distinct:.
  • Its elements apply in list order: the last upsert's values stay, a move repeat takes its transition only from a state in its from, and a delete repeat is skipped.
  • The interpreted target and synthesis apply it; generated Rust and Go keep the command an obligation, and ess verify diff reports declaring it as widening.

Per-file digest stamps​

  • A generated file's stamp carries its own contract digest only, so a change to one entity rewrites the files whose model slice holds it and leaves every other file byte for byte.
  • The whole-model digest is recorded once per generation, as model on each projection's owner in .ess-output/state.json.

UI documents​

  • A client row filter may search text, row.x contains state.search, so a list the server sends whole draws its search box again.
  • A tags field takes suggests: {reads, value} and offers the values of a read.
  • ess-ui-test/1 checks a form toggle's state with expect: {at: …, checked: true}, and a page header's help is a node a test opens and reads.
  • In the React target, an overlay opened from inside another stacks on it and keeps its draft, and an export saves the bytes the view's server answers.
  • In the terminal, a graph node action's confirm sits under its row, as the React project draws it.

UI documents gain a contains search, tag suggestions, toggle checks and a header help node.

items.content_html:
0.88 — Journeys reach every control, and a collection draws the controls it declares | ESS0.88.0 gives ess ui test a step for every control a page declares, makes the terminal and the generated React app send the same reorder and toggle payloads, draws the React collection's sort, expand, reorder, selection and column controls, and creates a further instance with the specification's input examples.ESSfield-noteessfield-noteadopterdevelopertry-spec-driven-developmentresearch

Source-owned field note · website/blog/2026-11-06-1200-journey-controls-and-collection-controls.md · revision 5c54de2902f8

0.88.0 changes the ess ui test journey runner, the terminal renderer, the generated React runtime and conformance synthesis. No source format moves, and a UI document renders as before unless it declares the collection controls the React runtime now draws. The gaps came from an ess ui test audit (#722), an adopter review of the React runtime (#723) and a synthesis report (#736). The changelog lists every change.

A journey reaches every control a page declares​

  • mark adds a row to its collection's selection, so a bulk action and its confirm run with act.
  • move: {at, to: up | down} moves a row of a collection with a reorder.
  • upload: {at, file} runs an upload action with a file named relative to the test file.
  • expect_export: {view, as?, params?} holds when an export read the view with those params.
  • open takes state, the page state a page keeps in its URL; a plain open starts without it.
  • act at a section form submits it, and at a sortable column sorts as its header does.
  • choose sets a form toggle, picks in a multiple choice field, a section-level choice and a filter bar's time window, and finds an option by its label however long it is.
  • select at a row's expand shows its detail.

The terminal and the React app send the same thing​

  • A reorder sends {id, delta} with delta -1 or 1 in both targets.
  • A toggle nobody touched is sent as its declared default, false when none is declared.
  • An upload is read as the browser reads it: a leading byte order mark is dropped, and text that is not UTF-8 is decoded with replacement characters.
  • In the terminal, h, l and i stay the view's own keys, so a filter-bar or form action never takes them.

A collection draws the controls it declares​

  • A client sort orders numbers by value, and mixed columns in one total order.
  • A wide table scrolls inside its frame, and its row actions take a column headed Actions.
  • Cards and lists draw the declared sort, the select-all and each row's actions.
  • expand draws an expand control, reorder a drag handle that moves a row one place within its group, selection: multiple a select-all and bulk_actions a bulk menu.
  • Item and toggle columns get their own column, and a default column subset draws only its columns.

Synthesis​

  • A second, suffixed instance is created with the input examples the specification gives, and a value a branch decision reads stays told apart between instances.

CI​

  • The go-task install retries its download, so a transient release download error no longer fails a test shard.

items.summary: 0.88.0 gives `ess ui test` a step for every control a page declares, makes the terminal and the generated React app send the same reorder and toggle payloads, draws the React collection's sort, expand, reorder, selection and column controls, and creates a further instance with the specification's input examples.

items.content_html:
0.87 — UI values render in their declared form, and synthesis refuses a misplaced not-found once | ESS0.87.0 renders each ess-ui/1 value in the form its field declares, durations and byte counts included, shows a choice's placeholder and a form's help, refuses a not-found branch declared after a guarded move once with its repair, and lets a journey find a row toggle again.ESSfield-noteessfield-noteadopterdevelopertry-spec-driven-developmentresearch

Source-owned field note · website/blog/2026-11-05-1200-ui-durations-help-and-synthesis-refusals.md · revision 5c54de2902f8

0.87.0 changes the ess-ui/1 grammar, the generated React runtime, the terminal renderer, the ess ui test journey runner, conformance synthesis and the OpenAPI projection's wording. No source format moves, and a UI document that uses none of the new keys renders as before. A downstream adopter reported most of the UI gaps (#723). The changelog lists every change; this note covers each of them.

A value renders in the form its field declares​

  • A field as: duration takes unit: ms | s, default ms, and shows h:mm:ss. Hours are never folded into days, and part of a second is dropped. A form input keeps the number.
  • A field as: bytes and a metric format: bytes show B, KB, MB or GB in 1024 steps.
  • In React, a date field shows an epoch-milliseconds value as a date, audio renders a player, link an anchor, a tag holding an object its label, a json input sends parsed JSON and a list input edits a list.
  • A placeholder read's fixture: resolves inside the document's fixtures.dir.

Choices, filter bars and forms show what they declare​

  • A choice takes placeholder:, shown while nothing is chosen and as a dropdown's empty option. It is named by the declared label of the field or action it picks for.
  • A filter bar's reset is true or {label}. Its search box is drawn only when a read on the page takes the search's state.
  • A form group and a field take help: {text, link}; a field's help is shown with its input and on its column header.
  • A form with save: on_change saves each change and shows no submit button.
  • Help links and the link primitive load only http, https, mailto or relative addresses; any other address is shown as text.

Tables and journeys​

  • ess ui run --tui no longer cuts a table column at 28 cells while the table has room.
  • ess ui test finds a row toggle again in either state. Since 0.86.0 the terminal writes a toggle's hint with its state mark, and every journey step on a toggle failed.

Synthesis​

  • An external: branch declared after an accepting when: branch that claims every input is refused once, as ESS-SYNTH-003, with its repair: declare it first with before_row: true, or narrow the guard. It was also refused as ESS-SYNTH-019, which called it a defect in ess.
  • A value type with invariants that nothing reaches is named in a note instead of being refused as ESS-SYNTH-013.

OpenAPI​

  • ess generate openapi calls an event published to consumers only when the component lists it under publishes:.

items.summary: 0.87.0 renders each ess-ui/1 value in the form its field declares, durations and byte counts included, shows a choice's placeholder and a form's help, refuses a not-found branch declared after a guarded move once with its repair, and lets a journey find a row toggle again.

items.content_html:
0.86 — UI documents label their values, show a toggle's state and page by size | ESS0.86.0 closes four gaps a downstream adopter of ess-ui/1 reported: a field or badge shows a declared label for each value, a row toggle shows the state it flips, a server-paged collection gains a page-size control and a pager footer, and a refused document is reported at the refused node's own path.ESSfield-noteessfield-noteadopterdevelopertry-spec-driven-developmentresearch

Source-owned field note · website/blog/2026-11-03-2200-ui-labels-toggles-pager-and-refusal-paths.md · revision 5c54de2902f8

0.86.0 changes the ess-ui/1 grammar, its checks, the generated React runtime and the terminal renderer. No source format moves, and a UI document that uses none of the new keys renders as before. A downstream adopter reported the gaps (#723). The changelog lists every change; this note covers each of them.

A value shows its declared label​

  • labels: on a field or a badge primitive gives the text shown for each value. It is either a map written out or the name of an entry of the new document-level label_maps. Booleans are keyed "true" and "false".
  • A value the map does not name shows its raw value. A badge keeps the raw value in its class and its tone.
  • A choice column with fixed options shows each option's label.
  • ess ui check reports a name that resolves to no map (label_map_refs) and a map nothing names (label_map_unused).
  • Labels are declared, never derived from a field name.

A toggle shows the state it flips​

  • A row toggle that runs a command used to render off on every row. It now takes its state from an optional checked: expression, or else from its one bind entry written not <expr>.
  • A does: toggle with neither warns toggle_state_unknown.
  • checked: without as: toggle is refused (checked_needs_toggle).
  • React and the terminal read the same expression.
  • A column as: toggle renders a switch, not the text true or false.

A server-paged collection has a page-size control​

  • A read with paging: server takes pager: {page, size, sizes}, naming the read params that carry the page and the page size. sizes defaults to [25, 50, 100].
  • The footer shows Previous, the page (and of how many when the total is known) and Next.
  • With a size, the footer adds a per-page select that sets the size and returns to page 1.
  • The footer writes the state paths the params bind, never a fixed state.page.
  • ess ui check refuses a pager it cannot honour: one without server paging, a param that is not bound to a state path, page and size on overlapping paths, an empty size list, or a pager on any read but a collection's.

A refusal is reported where it is​

  • A refused node is reported at its own path. Before, a list entry whose name or field matched a key the schema holds an action under was read as that action and reported first.
  • A refused key in a section's states is reported at that state.
  • An export's params may be a map beside the single expression. selection.<field> is allowed only on a bulk action (export_selection).
  • An empty state may carry a title.
items.title: 0.86 — UI documents label their values, show a toggle's state and page by size
items.summary: 0.86.0 closes four gaps a downstream adopter of ess-ui/1 reported: a field or badge shows a declared label for each value, a row toggle shows the state it flips, a server-paged collection gains a page-size control and a pager footer, and a refused document is reported at the refused node's own path.

items.content_html:
0.85 — Every witness reads back its effect, and the mutation audit covers grants | ESS0.85.0 adds format ess/34, in which a compensating refusal may delete its row and a named refusal requires the row it addressed unchanged. The mutation audit gains two grant classes, lists the sites it could not mutate and runs on the scenario clock. Go synthesis, the clap target and the generated explorers fix six defects.ESSfield-noteessfield-noteadopterdevelopertry-spec-driven-developmentresearch

Source-owned field note · website/blog/2026-11-03-1200-every-witness-reads-back-and-the-audit-covers-grants.md · revision 5c54de2902f8

0.85.0 adds one source format, ess/34, and moves the mutation report to ess-mutation-report/8 and the manifest to ess-mutation-manifest/7 where they list something new. A model with nothing new keeps its bytes. The changelog lists every change; this note covers each of them.

Every witness reads back its effect​

  • From ess/34 a compensating refusal (compensates: true beside external:) may delete its addressed row with deletes: and instance:. Its scenario requires the error, no event and the row absent from every immediate view.
  • From ess/34 a named when: or when_related: refusal of a command addressing an existing row snapshots that row completely and requires it unchanged. Below it, suites keep their bytes.
  • At every format, a further witness of a deleting branch requires the deleted row absent, and a guard's boundary row for a deletes: branch is sent for a row of its own.
  • A non-refusing unknown_instance: branch must store no row with the identity it was sent.
  • A view row field set from an Optional<T> input through its declared conversion is asserted at the value sent.

The mutation audit covers grants and lists its gaps​

  • Two new classes audit actor grants: grant-drop removes one command from one actor's may:, grant-add gives an actor one served command it lacks (#710). Where either is selected, the baseline and every mutant's suite keep their <command>/grant/denied scenarios.
  • Each site a selected class excluded or could not mutate is listed with its reason under unmutated_sites, in the text, the report and the manifest (#711). The summary says how many of the sites considered were scored. --fail-on-unmutated makes such a site block exit 0; the default exit status is unchanged.
  • error-swap mutates a refusal that carries its error's payload, re-keying the entry to the error swapped in (#709).
  • --target interpreted runs synthesized scenarios on the scenario clock run uses, so a model with a now guard is scored.

Go synthesis and the generated explorers​

  • Go synthesis copies a required event field into an Optional command input as a pointer, and writes a served component named server or wire under a repaired file name instead of panicking.
  • --target clap generates one tree with every group of the components that share a cli.binary; validation refuses a group, command or view two of them both declare.
  • The generated explorers agree with the interpreter on an external: branch for a stored row, fail an answer that leaves out a required response member, and explore only the scoped component's commands and views.
items.title: 0.85 — Every witness reads back its effect, and the mutation audit covers grants
items.summary: 0.85.0 adds format ess/34, in which a compensating refusal may delete its row and a named refusal requires the row it addressed unchanged. The mutation audit gains two grant classes, lists the sites it could not mutate and runs on the scenario clock. Go synthesis, the clap target and the generated explorers fix six defects.

items.content_html:
0.84 — Generated servers refuse what their OpenAPI refuses, and generated UIs call their binding's routes | ESS0.84.0 adds no format: generated Rust servers refuse a malformed Timestamp and an undeclared JSON member at decode, authored success acts assert that no error came back, denied-grant scenarios reach ranked views and every ungranted actor, and a generated UI calls the routes its HTTP binding serves.ESSfield-noteessfield-noteadopterdevelopertry-spec-driven-developmentresearch

Source-owned field note · website/blog/2026-11-03-0900-generated-servers-refuse-what-their-openapi-refuses.md · revision 5c54de2902f8

0.84.0 adds no source, scenario or suite format. It changes what generated servers admit, what an authored success step checks, which denied-grant scenarios synthesis writes, and how generated UIs reach a server. The changelog lists every change; this note covers each of them.

Generated servers refuse what their OpenAPI refuses​

  • The generated Rust codecs refuse at decode, before anything is stored, a Timestamp that is not an RFC 3339 date-time and a member a closed JSON object does not declare. The server answers 400, or the binding's refusals.malformed, naming the member's path (#707).
  • Before, the server stored the text or dropped the member, while the OpenAPI document it serves already refused the body. A struct declaring undeclared_fields: ignored and a Json value stay open.
  • The same decoders read the log, so decode_system_event refuses an envelope an older server wrote with a free-text Timestamp or an extra member in a closed struct.
  • The generated Go server refuses a top-level JSON command member no input field names, on bound and derived routes, and reads a Timestamp with the same grammar as the Rust server.
  • Known limit: an Optional member sent as null is still taken as absent by the generated Rust server, while its served OpenAPI refuses the body. It is tracked as a backlog story.

An authored success act asserts no error​

  • An authored act whose outcome: names a branch that declares no error now also requires that no error came back. A target answering the success branch under its own name with an error fails the step; it used to pass on the outcome name alone.
  • No suite format moves. A library caller assembling an authored suite by hand selects the format with select_fresh_format_for and runs it with Runner::run_admitted, as the CLI does.

Denied-grant scenarios​

  • Synthesis writes <command>/grant/denied for a command acting on an existing row beside a view ranked by order_by (#712).
  • <view>/grant/read/denied reads the view as every ungranted actor of the view's own domain, then as no actor. Before, it read one actor of any domain, so a target admitting an ungranted actor of the view's domain passed.

Generated UIs call their binding's routes​

  • ess generate ui and ess ui run --tui take --http <binding>: the generated route table carries the method and path the ess-http/1 binding declares, so the UI calls the routes the server generated for the same binding serves (#713).
  • A command served on get is sent without a body, and React refuses a path value of . or ...

Renderer fixes​

  • The terminal renderer addresses a row action's confirm by the view's row key, and a record's actions see the row the record shows.
  • An account menu entry keeps its sets and navigate in React. ess ui check refuses an entry a renderer would drop, an entry that does not read as an action, and sets beside does, navigate or opens.
items.title: 0.84 — Generated servers refuse what their OpenAPI refuses, and generated UIs call their binding's routes
items.summary: 0.84.0 adds no format: generated Rust servers refuse a malformed Timestamp and an undeclared JSON member at decode, authored success acts assert that no error came back, denied-grant scenarios reach ranked views and every ungranted actor, and a generated UI calls the routes its HTTP binding serves.

items.content_html:
0.83 — Optional list appends, binding refusals that check event identities, and refusals that tell states apart | ESS0.83.0 adds no format: the interpreted target appends null for an absent optional list element, binding refusal scenarios compare their trigger event's identities, a row-set guard beside named rows is witnessed on every refusal order, and no-view input refusals tell the record's state apart.ESSfield-noteessfield-noteadopterdevelopertry-spec-driven-developmentresearch

Source-owned field note · website/blog/2026-11-02-1400-optional-appends-and-refusals-that-tell-states-apart.md · revision 5c54de2902f8

0.83.0 adds no source, scenario or suite format, and every change in it is a fix. One is in the interpreted target, and the others are in the conformance suites synthesis writes. The changelog lists every change; this note covers each of them.

Appending an absent optional element​

  • The interpreted target appends null for an absent or null element of {append: input.<field>} over a List<Optional<T>>, as generated Rust and Go already append None and nil. Synthesis expects that null in the view row.
  • Before, the interpreted target refused the command as unsupported.
  • An element over a list of required elements is unchanged.

Binding refusal scenarios compare event identities​

  • A synthesized binding refusal scenario covers a refusal the binding's policy drops, escalates or retries a bounded number of times. It now compares the identity fields of the trigger's event with the instances its invocation was sent, as the other binding scenarios do since 0.82.0.
  • It also compares them with each id the invocation was sent as a literal for a field of an entity's identity type, such as the id a trigger naming no related row is sent. That holds where it sends another publisher of the event, or a trigger naming a row arranged so the predicate refuses it.
  • Before, it expected that event by shape alone, so a target publishing a wrong id there passed.
  • The suite bytes of seven fixture models move; the changelog names them.

A row set beside named rows, on every refusal order​

  • A command guarding on a row set beside rows its input names (ess/32) is witnessed on every refusal order.
  • A refusal over a named row that also carries a when: is held beside the row set's rows with a send that holds that when:. Where the when: equates two inputs, that send names one row twice. Where no such send stands, the refusal is witnessed on its related row alone, so its row-set branch is no longer refused.
  • A row-set refusal is held beside a later refusal whose when: compares the named rows. Where only a creator sent one row twice lays the selected row, that is how it is laid.
  • A forall on the accepting branch is held on a selected row the forall passes, and its default refusal on a selected row naming the send's own rows. A target refusing on any selected row now fails, at ess/31 too.

No-view input refusals tell the record's state apart​

  • These are input refusals on a command that addresses an existing record, on a model where no identity view shows the row.
  • The arranged half of such a refusal tells the arranged state apart from every other state. Where the first branch addressing the record from that state also runs from other states, the scenario sends the shortest sequence a bounded search finds that does tell them apart. Where the bound stops the search first, that sequence is extended one send at a time past it. It is drawn from the command's branches and from other commands whose input names only that record, with a wrong_state: refusal among the answers. A free-text input beside the identity names no record.
  • A refusal beside held-state branches reads the record back after each held-state send, through sends from that state that tell it apart from every other state. The command's own branches come first, its held-state refusals among them.
  • A target that moves the record on refusal and publishes nothing now fails both. Before, they required only the error and no event, and such a target passed.
  • Where the sends tried leave states untold, the scenario is withdrawn and refused as ESS-SYNTH-001, naming the states left. Where no send has a valid input, it names every branch tried.
  • A model with an identity view keeps its suite bytes. The test model occurrence-clock-offers.yaml, which has none, moves its suite bytes: its AcceptOffer/outcome/malformed scenario reads the offer back in each of its three states, with its scenario count and refusals unchanged.
items.title: 0.83 — Optional list appends, binding refusals that check event identities, and refusals that tell states apart
items.summary: 0.83.0 adds no format: the interpreted target appends null for an absent optional list element, binding refusal scenarios compare their trigger event's identities, a row-set guard beside named rows is witnessed on every refusal order, and no-view input refusals tell the record's state apart.

items.content_html:
0.82 — Binding scenarios that check event identities, refusals that probe the record, and validation that names the file | ESS0.82.0 adds no format: synthesized binding scenarios compare the identity fields of their trigger event, the arranged half of a refusal without an identity view probes the record through the command, and ess specify validate names the file a refusal was read from.ESSfield-noteessfield-noteadopterdevelopertry-spec-driven-developmentresearch

Source-owned field note · website/blog/2026-11-01-2200-event-identities-and-file-cited-refusals.md · revision 5c54de2902f8

0.82.0 adds no source, scenario or suite format, and every change in it is a fix. Two are in the conformance suites synthesis writes, and one is in what ess specify validate cites. The changelog lists every change; this note covers each of them.

Binding scenarios compare event identities​

  • Synthesized binding scenarios compare the identity fields of the trigger's event with the instances its invocation was sent, or with the row it acts on. That covers flow, mapping, delivery, on-failure, a bounded retry's attempts and final failure, an unbounded retry selected per refusal, and a condition's negative witnesses.
  • The comparison also holds where the binding arranges a row before it, as command scenarios have done since beyond10x/ess#273.
  • A target that publishes another identity in the event now fails these scenarios. Before, it passed them.
  • A model whose binding triggers carry no captured instance into their event keeps its suite bytes.

The arranged half of a refusal probes the record​

  • This is the arranged half of an input refusal, on a command that addresses an existing record, where no identity view shows the arranged row. After the refused send, the scenario sends a valid input for that record. That input belongs to the first branch that addresses the record from the state it was arranged in, and the scenario requires that branch to answer.
  • A target that moves the record out of every state that branch runs from on refusal, or otherwise changes what it answers, and publishes nothing, now fails. Before, the scenario required only the error and no event, and such a target passed. A move between two states that branch runs from is still not seen.
  • Where no such branch has a valid send, the scenario is withdrawn and refused as ESS-SYNTH-001, naming the branches tried (beyond10x/ess#209).
  • A model with an identity view keeps its suite bytes.

Validation names the file​

  • ess specify validate on a specification of several files names the file a refusal was read from. Before, it named <document> whenever the refused declaration's name was written in more than one file, as a name declared in two files is.
  • A refusal made while a file is read is cited in that file. One checked after assembly is cited in the file of the copy assembly kept, which is the second when the first does not convert. A name written twice in one file names the file and no line.
  • The library's Specification::assemble_traced and resolve::diagnose_traced return and read that record; diagnose_locating is unchanged.

items.summary: 0.82.0 adds no format: synthesized binding scenarios compare the identity fields of their trigger event, the arranged half of a refusal without an identity view probes the record through the command, and ess specify validate names the file a refusal was read from.

0.81 — Nullable Binary64 fields in generated types, name aliases in the schema, and synthesis that follows bindings | ESS0.81.0 adds no format: ess generate types realizes a nullable optional Binary64 field and refuses the response root of a command without a response by name, the published schema admits the id: and component: name aliases, and synthesis sends related-row and wrong-state scenarios to rows that keep their branch.ESSfield-noteessfield-noteadopterdevelopertry-spec-driven-developmentresearch

Source-owned field note · website/blog/2026-11-01-1600-nullable-binary64-and-binding-aware-synthesis.md · revision 5c54de2902f8

0.81.0 adds no source, scenario or suite format, and every change in it is a fix. Two are in ess generate types, one is in the published document schema, and three are in how synthesis picks the rows a scenario is sent to. The changelog lists every change; this note covers each of them.

Generated types​

  • An Optional<Binary64> field declared presence: null_when_absent or omitted_or_null is realized as Rust and Go, in a declared struct and in a command's input or response root. Its Binary64 location is the number member of the field's anyOf [number, null]; before, it was the property, and realization was refused as model_binary64_layout.
  • The TypeScript report names its model_binary64 obligation at that member.
  • --root <command>.response on a command that declares no response is refused as unknown_root, naming the command and saying it declares no response, as --all-commands leaves it out. Before, it generated an empty object type.

Name aliases in the published schema​

  • schemas/generated/ess.schema.json admits a binding's name written id: and a component's written component:, the aliases the parser already reads, each with the same charset as name:. Before, it refused every document that spelt a name that way.
  • Writing both spellings, or neither, is refused, as the parser refuses it. Parsing is unchanged.

Synthesis​

  • A when_related: branch is no longer sent for a related row that only a step setting off a binding selects, where that binding's command writes a field or the state the guard reads, or removes the row. Such a row is passed over for one no binding rewrites; where none is found, the branch is refused as ESS-SYNTH-003 naming the step, the binding and the command it invokes.
  • A when_related: command whose input is chosen for an external branch, where the precedence plan reads the related row's exists: false before the addressed row's existence or held state, sends its unknown-identity scenario and its held-state refusals beside a present related row. Before, it sent a reference no row carries and the target answered exists: false instead of the refusal.
  • A model with such a command and no wrong_state: moves its suite bytes: its held-state refusals now name a present row, so the held state is what refuses them. Every other model keeps its bytes.
  • A wrong-state scenario of a command reading stored fields is sent to a row its moving branch's own when_subject: holds on, and to a row holding a value in every field a sibling's stored guard reads, so no absent field stops selection before the wrong-state answer. Where no reachable row serves, the scenario is refused as ESS-SYNTH-003 naming the guard.
  • A model whose bindings write nothing a related guard reads keeps its suite bytes.

0.80 — HTTP-bound inputs and short names in generated types, and input-type rules in Entity Runtime | ESS0.80.0 adds no format: ess generate types takes --http, so a command's input type is the request body its bound OpenAPI document publishes, --names short combines with --all-commands and --all-views, and Entity Runtime lowering keeps an unstored input type's rules.ESSfield-noteessfield-noteadopterdevelopertry-spec-driven-developmentresearch

Source-owned field note · website/blog/2026-11-01-1200-http-bound-inputs-and-short-names.md · revision 5c54de2902f8

0.80.0 adds no source, scenario or suite format. It changes what ess generate types writes under two flags, what Entity Runtime lowering does with a command input's type, and how synthesis decides an identity guard. The changelog lists every change; this note covers each of them.

Generated types for an HTTP binding​

  • ess generate types takes --http <binding> (and --refines), compiled as ess generate --kind openapi --http compiles it (beyond10x/ess#656).
  • Under it each <command>.input is the request body the bound OpenAPI document publishes, without the fields its route carries in the path, so the Rust, Go and TypeScript types decode that body.
  • A command whose route publishes no body (encoded query, or every field in the path) has no input root: --root <command>.input is refused as unpublished_body, naming the command and why, and --all-commands leaves it out.
  • Responses and view rows are unchanged, and without --http every generated file keeps its bytes.

Short names for every command and view​

  • ess generate types --names short combines with --all-commands and --all-views (beyond10x/ess#409).
  • A command's input or response and a view's row are named by their owner's last segment and the member: demo.notes.Create.input is CreateInput and demo.notes.ByOwner.row is ByOwnerRow. Before, every input shortened to Input and every row to Row, and two commands or views were refused as short_name_collision.
  • Declared type and event short names are unchanged, and two commands of one name in two domains are still refused, naming both.

Input-type rules in Entity Runtime​

  • Entity Runtime lowering no longer drops the invariants: and prefix: of a command input's type unless every accepting branch stores the input in a field of that type.
  • An update holds them as operation preconditions over $args.input.<field>, lowered as a guard is, so an ordering over a Timestamp becomes before/after.
  • A creation, which has no precondition in entity-core, and an ordering over text, which entity-core cannot decide, are refused as InputInvariantUnsupported, naming the input.

Synthesis fix​

  • A when: guard on the identity input of a row a branch is sent for, below a non-creating unknown_instance: or on the subject the branch acts on, is decided on the identity of the row the scenario arranges, a compound guard by its identity parts (beyond10x/ess#645, beyond10x/ess#693).
  • The row's creator is steered onto an identity that keeps the branch; where none does, the branch is refused as ESS-SYNTH-003 naming the guard. Before, the scenario was sent a row of another identity and the target answered another branch.
  • A related row's boundary run that would create a second row under such an identity gives way to the next branch answering there, where the whole scenario was refused as ESS-SYNTH-001.
  • A boundary run that sends such an identity input another value, or follows a branch that deleted the row, is sent a row of that identity, or is refused naming the guard and not sent. Before, it was sent an identity no row carries and the target answered unknown.

0.79 — Nested-member claims, Binary64 in conformance suites, and typed authored inputs | ESS0.79.0 adds scenario format ess-scenario/6 and suite pair ess-conformance/62 and /63: an authored claim may name a nested member by its path, an authored literal input is held to its type, and a model that reaches a finite Binary64 runs a conformance suite.ESSfield-noteessfield-noteadopterdevelopertry-spec-driven-developmentresearch

Source-owned field note · website/blog/2026-11-01-0130-nested-claims-and-binary64.md · revision 5c54de2902f8

0.79.0 adds no source format: a specification keeps its meaning, its IR bytes and its compiled digest. It adds scenario format ess-scenario/6 and suite pair ess-conformance/62 (ordinary) and /63 (coverage). The changelog lists every change; this note covers what the new formats carry and the fixes that came with them.

Nested-member claims​

  • From ess-scenario/6 a claim in an act's response:, an event's payload:, an error's fields: or a row may name one member of a nested value by its dotted path, checkpoint.checkpoint_id: cp-1, under one rule on all four surfaces: a field is claimed whole or by its paths, not both.
  • A response path is carried by ess-conformance/62 and /63; event, error and row paths compile to dotted keys older suites already read, so those suites keep their format.
  • A partial nested literal in a response: is refused as ESS-AUTHOR-014, naming each member it leaves out at its path.

Binary64 through a conformance suite​

  • A model that reaches a Binary64 in an entity's fields, a command's input or response, an event's or error's fields, or a view now synthesizes, authors and runs a suite at ess-conformance/62 (coverage /63).
  • Rust, Go and TypeScript compare it by its nearest binary64 under IEEE equality (-0 equals 0); a token with no finite image, such as 1e400, is refused by name. An authored Binary64 literal of magnitude 2^53 or more is refused as ESS-AUTHOR-015, because view and event assertions compare an integer token exactly.
  • A Binary64 reached through an entity identity, a view parameter, an actor attribute, a binding or a conversion is still refused (ESS-AUTHOR-036).

Authored inputs meet their type​

  • From ess-scenario/6 an act's literal input that its declared type refuses, at any depth and beside an $instance reference, is refused as ESS-AUTHOR-015 at its member path.
  • A refusal guard that only out-of-type inputs meet is refused as ESS-SYNTH-003, naming the field, the type and the constraint.

Synthesis fixes​

  • Both branches of a != or == guard that compares an input with its own example: are written, for text, Uuid, Timestamp, Duration and Bytes, and for a struct member a structured example reaches.
  • An input-guarded refusal beside exhaustive held-state branches, and the byte-length children of an any over alphabet-bounded texts, are witnessed where they were refused.
  • An accepting branch read after unknown_instance: is arranged with its row stored first; guards on related identities, parent rows and cascades get the rows they read.
  • An authored scenario that repeats a key in a mapping is refused as ESS-AUTHOR-047.

0.78 — Structured input examples, rows a deployment provides, and lifecycle summaries | ESS0.78.0 adds source format ess/33: a struct, map or Json input may carry an example, an entity may declare that the deployment provides its rows, and lifecycle transitions and states may carry a summary.ESSfield-noteessfield-noteadopterdevelopertry-spec-driven-developmentresearch

Source-owned field note · website/blog/2026-10-31-1600-structured-examples-and-provided-rows.md · revision 5c54de2902f8

0.78.0 adds source format ess/33. A model that does not use its new keys keeps its meaning, its IR bytes and its compiled digest. The changelog lists every change; this note covers what ess/33 adds and the fixes that came with it.

Structured input examples​

  • An input typed as a struct (open or closed), a Map<…> or Json, through any newtype or Optional, may carry an example:. Synthesis sends it at the plain instance; a struct example reaches synthesis through its declared members, so a guard reading one keeps the scenario that refutes it.
  • An open struct's example keeps the members it does not declare, and the interpreted target now admits those members in a command input at every format.

Rows a deployment provides​

  • An entity may declare provided: true: the deployment holds its rows, and no command of the specification need create one.
  • Where a when_related: {via: input.<field>} guard reads such a row and no declared outcome creates it, the scenario resolves an entity fixture {name, type, entity, state} before it runs (suite formats ess-conformance/60 and /61). The interpreted target creates the row; the Go and TypeScript runtimes pass the entity and state to their fixture provider.
  • fixture_inputs: is refused over every input a guard reads, including the identity a related-row guard reads.

Lifecycle summaries​

  • A transition may carry a one-line summary:, and a state may carry one in its mapping form, {name, wire?, summary?}. ess verify diff reports a moved transition summary as transition-summary-changed (ess-diff/22), compatible.
  • A flat summary:, wire:, display: or code: on a named type is refused with a message naming naming: {summary: …}.

0.77 — Alike HTTP outcomes, wider OpenAPI import, and branches an earlier refusal hides | ESS0.77.0 lets an HTTP route answer two outcomes alike, imports open objects from OpenAPI, keeps declared field order in generated types on request, and refuses a branch an earlier refusal always answers first.ESSfield-noteessfield-noteadopterdevelopertry-spec-driven-developmentresearch

Source-owned field note · website/blog/2026-10-29-1100-alike-outcomes-and-unreachable-branches.md · revision 5c54de2902f8

0.77.0 is a feature release with no new source format: every model keeps its meaning, its IR bytes and its compiled digest. The changelog lists every change since 0.70.0; this note covers 0.77.0 and the releases since the last note.

HTTP bindings​

  • A route may declare alike: groups of outcomes whose answers are equal, so two outcomes share a status and a body instead of being refused as indistinguishable; OpenAPI writes one response naming every member (#652).
  • An outcome may answer a String field as text/plain with encoding: text. A route may declare its own refusals:, a literal or empty body for empty, and body: array for a view that is not paged (#673).

Import and generated types​

  • OpenAPI import admits open objects, the empty and true schemas as JSON values, and a nullable anyOf/oneOf pair as an optional value (#647).
  • ess generate schema types-bundle --integer-format-widths realizes int32 and int64 at native width (#648).
  • ess generate types --declared-field-order keeps the order the specification declares, and --rust-box-only-recursion boxes only the references that close a cycle (#661). Without these options the output keeps its bytes.
  • Rust and web synthesis accept a response field that shares a name with an input field (#659).

Validation and mutation​

  • ess specify validate refuses a when: branch whose input guard implies the guard of an input-guarded refusal answered before it, as unreachable_branch (#702). Before, only synthesis reported it.
  • ess verify conform mutate scores a precedence swap of two guards no input selects together as equivalent, also for wide enums, membership lists and disjunctions (#703).

Since 0.70.0​

  • 0.76.0: schemas publish entity invariants and Binary64, text length and distinct-list bounds as keywords; a defined / not defined pair of branches is exhaustive without a default; ess-composition/5 compares events, commands, constraints and variant attributes; HTTP bindings name operation ids and servers.
  • 0.75.0: the workspace builds on its declared minimum Rust version again, and seeded synthesis explains the seeds it cannot use.
  • 0.74.0: seeds are admitted for models whose actors declare caller attributes.
  • 0.71.0 to 0.73.0: synthesis covers more set updates, deletes, bindings and related-row guards that it refused before.

items.summary: 0.77.0 lets an HTTP route answer two outcomes alike, imports open objects from OpenAPI, keeps declared field order in generated types on request, and refuses a branch an earlier refusal always answers first.

0.70 — Named rows beside a row set, state wire spellings, and replays that finish | ESS0.70.0 adds source format ess/32: one command may guard on rows its input names beside a row-set guard, a struct may declare no fields, and a lifecycle state may declare its wire spelling.ESSfield-noteessfield-noteadopterdevelopertry-spec-driven-developmentresearch

Source-owned field note · website/blog/2026-10-26-2000-named-rows-beside-a-row-set.md · revision 5c54de2902f8

0.70.0 is a feature release. It adds the source format ess/32 and the suite formats ess-conformance/58 and /59. A model below ess/32 keeps its meaning, its IR bytes and its compiled digest. The changelog lists every change since 0.63.0.

Rows the input names, beside a row set​

From ess/32 one command may guard on rows its input names, when_related: {via: input.<field>, …}, beside a row-set guard, when_related: {entity, where, …}. "Connect two ports that exist and face the right way, unless a wire already leaves the source" is one command. A missing named row answers first, then every refusal over a present named row or a row set in declaration order, then the accepting branches (#554).

More in ess/32​

  • A struct may declare fields: [], open or closed (#649).
  • A lifecycle state may declare its wire spelling, states: [{name: Indexing, wire: indexing}], and two variants of one enum spelled alike on the wire are refused (#639).

Conformance and generated code​

  • ess verify conform synthesize no longer stops with InvalidReplay at ess/26 and later.
  • A view may publish a Decimal, compared by value; such a suite is ess-conformance/58 or /59.
  • A create-or-update command beside a related-row refusal gets a scenario for every branch (#641).
  • The synthesized Rust server decodes published events and returns the events a call published.
  • A variant's code: names its generated identifier, and a dotted label such as call.started synthesizes (#662).
  • ess generate types --check compares what it would write with --out (#654).

0.63 — Values computed by typed expressions, and one precedence order for guards | ESS0.63.0 adds source format ess/27: a value may be computed by a typed expression, a guard may read a digest of its input, and every command's guards answer in one precedence order.ESSfield-noteessfield-noteadopterdevelopertry-spec-driven-developmentresearch

Source-owned field note · website/blog/2026-10-19-1200-typed-expressions-and-one-precedence-order.md · revision 5c54de2902f8

0.63.0 is a feature release. It adds the source format ess/27, the suite formats ess-conformance/52 and /53, the delta format ess-diff/20 and the suite comparison ess-suite-diff/1. A model below ess/27 keeps its meaning, its IR bytes and its compiled digest. The changelog lists every change since 0.59.0.

Values computed by typed expressions​

From ess/27 a value in sets:, an event's payload: or an error's payload: may be computed by an expression, {expr: "<expression>"}, and a view field may be computed from its source row, such as expr: "ended_at - started_at". Arithmetic over Integer and Decimal is exact, / is an Optional<Decimal> that is absent at a zero divisor, round rounds a quotient once, and Timestamp - Timestamp is a Duration. Synthesis runs the branch again on inputs worth checking the figure on: a zero divisor and a rounding tie either way (#560).

A guard may read a fact through a digest or encoding function: challenge != base64url(sha256(ascii(input.verifier))) states a PKCE S256 check as a held-row predicate (#584).

One precedence order​

Under ess/27 a branch answers in the order of what it must read: the request alone, then whether the addressed record exists, then what it holds, then the rows around it, then the accepting branches (#554). Every guard pair once refused for want of an order now validates, such as when_related: beside when_subject: or wrong_state: (#282).

More in ess/27​

  • shorthand: <field> on a struct type lets a value be written as that one field (#594).
  • An each: entry of affects: may move or delete the row each element names (#596).
  • A binding condition may compare a Boolean leaf with true or false.

Conformance​

  • ess verify conform diff --from <suite> --to <suite> says which scenarios two suites add, remove and change, and --format json writes an ess-suite-diff/1 document (#572).
  • ess verify conform synthesize --check compares what it would write with what is committed (#571).
  • Suites ess-conformance/52 and /53 state the event catalog once at the root instead of in every scenario, check a value type's invariants inside a view's lists, maps, optionals and unions, and await a command the system issues itself (#570, #542).

0.59 — An authored act states the caller its command is sent as | ESS0.59.0 lets an authored scenario state the caller attributes its command reads, and fixes two cases where synthesis refused or mis-chose a scenario.ESSfield-noteessfield-noteadopterdevelopertry-spec-driven-developmentresearch

Source-owned field note · website/blog/2026-10-11-0230-authored-caller-attributes.md · revision 5c54de2902f8

0.59.0 is a feature release. It adds the authored scenario format ess-scenario/5; specifications, suites and deltas keep their formats. The changelog lists every change since 0.55.0.

An authored act states its caller​

An act in an ess-scenario/5 document states the caller its command is sent as, under caller:. Each attribute value is a literal of its declared type, or {$instance: name} for an instance arranged with setup:. A command that records {caller: account_id} now runs from an authored scenario on the interpreted target and the generated Go and TypeScript runners.

  • ess verify conform author refuses an attribute the act's actor: does not declare (ESS-AUTHOR-013), a required attribute the command reads that the act leaves unstated (ESS-AUTHOR-014), and an instance captured at run time (ESS-AUTHOR-015), naming the attribute and the command.
  • An act with no caller: sends none, and its suite keeps its bytes. ess-scenario/1 to /4 refuse the key.
  • A suite step that reaches a caller attribute nothing supplied is still unsupported, now with a reason naming the attribute and caller:.

Synthesis​

  • A command whose branches a stored field of its subject selects (when_subject:) gets its scenarios even when no view observes that field; synthesis used to refuse each with ESS-SYNTH-001. A model with an immediate view covering the guarded fields keeps its suite byte for byte (#496).
  • A when_related: guard that reads a member of a struct input is decided against the key the subject was created under, where it used to choose a row against a key the search made up. A struct sent as a literal keeps its scenarios byte for byte (#521).
items.title: 0.59 — An authored act states the caller its command is sent as
items.summary: 0.59.0 lets an authored scenario state the caller attributes its command reads, and fixes two cases where synthesis refused or mis-chose a scenario.

0.55 — Json in CLI results, and optional values an implementation supplies | ESS0.55.0 lets a CLI result carry a JSON document as JSON, and routes an optional generated value through a port the implementation answers.ESSfield-noteessfield-noteadopterdevelopertry-spec-driven-developmentresearch

Source-owned field note · website/blog/2026-10-06-2200-json-cli-results-and-optional-generator-ports.md · revision 5c54de2902f8

0.55.0 is a feature release. Specifications, suites and deltas keep their formats. It follows 0.54.0, released the same day with source format ess/23; the changelog lists both.

A CLI result carries JSON as JSON​

A CLI result field may now be typed Json, alone or under Optional, List or a String-keyed Map. The generated adapter writes the value as JSON, so a caller parses the answer once instead of decoding JSON text out of a JSON answer.

  • The result check accepts any JSON value in that field and refuses a reply outside the declared shape as cli_result.
  • A Json input field is refused: an argv word has no JSON spelling a binding declares. A Json error field is refused too.
  • Generated CLI packages carry new src/wire.rs bytes, so ess generate cli --check reports drift until they are regenerated (beyond10x/ess#468).

An optional generated value comes from the implementation​

{generated: true} on a value of type Optional<T> used to be filled absent every time. From 0.55.0 the generated Rust and Go behaviours read it from a context port that answers an optional T, so a value that is absent only when there is nothing to report can reach the event.

  • The port is generate_optional_<t> returning Option<T> in Rust and GenerateOptional<T> returning *T in Go. A context that implements the port adds the method; the generated demonstration context answers it absent.
  • A field nothing sets stays absent and asks no port (beyond10x/ess#467).

items.summary: 0.55.0 lets a CLI result carry a JSON document as JSON, and routes an optional generated value through a port the implementation answers.

0.51 — Branches selected by existence, and output that regenerates anywhere | ESS0.51.0 generates the existence lookup a Rust server needs to choose between creating and refusing, and lets committed generated output regenerate in another checkout.ESSfield-noteessfield-noteadopterdevelopertry-spec-driven-developmentresearch

Source-owned field note · website/blog/2026-10-01-2330-existence-lookup-and-portable-output.md · revision 5c54de2902f8

0.51.0 is a feature and fix release. Specifications, suites and deltas keep their formats.

Branches selected by whether the record exists​

A command with an existing_instance: refusal beside a creation, or a creating unknown_instance: branch beside an update, needs to know whether the record is already stored. Until now the generated Rust server owed such a command as an obligation. From 0.51.0 it looks the input identity up in the storage port before dispatch and selects the branch itself.

  • A command whose lookup would not match its creations (another entity, another input field, an identity that is not an input) stays an obligation.
  • Go, Web and Clap still refuse both forms by name.
  • If your realization implemented one of these commands' …Behavior obligation, Generated<P> now runs the generated behaviour and no longer forwards that command to it (beyond10x/ess#310).

Committed output regenerates in another checkout​

Generated output committed with its .ess-output now regenerates in a clone, a second worktree or CI, under any umask, when its owned files still have their recorded bytes:

  • a regeneration that changes nothing leaves state.json byte-identical, and the first one that writes records the new root;
  • a state carried without matching files refuses, lists them, and prints the steps to re-enroll with ess generate output adopt;
  • a root replaced by a copy mid-transaction refuses recovery there (beyond10x/ess#306).
items.title: 0.51 — Branches selected by existence, and output that regenerates anywhere
items.summary: 0.51.0 generates the existence lookup a Rust server needs to choose between creating and refusing, and lets committed generated output regenerate in another checkout.

items.content_html:
0.50 — Aggregates over rows a when_related guard admits | ESS0.50.0 is one synthesis fix: an aggregate view whose creating command has a when_related guard gets its aggregate scenario instead of being refused with ESS-SYNTH-017.ESSfield-noteessfield-noteadopterdevelopertry-spec-driven-developmentresearch

Source-owned field note · website/blog/2026-10-01-2200-aggregates-over-related-guards.md · revision 5c54de2902f8

0.50.0 is a fix release. Specifications, suites and deltas keep their formats.

Aggregates over a when_related-guarded creator​

Until now, an aggregate view over rows created by a command with a when_related guard was refused with ESS-SYNTH-017: synthesis could not create the rows the view counts, because each needed a related row the guard would accept. From 0.50.0 the view gets its <view>/aggregate scenario:

  • each row's related row is arranged first, and rows given one value of the guard's input share it;
  • every input a guard predicate compares with the related row's owner link names an owner that is arranged too;
  • a group key read from a related row's owner link holds one owner per value, so a target that groups under the wrong owner fails.

Where a row still cannot be arranged, the refusal names the reason (beyond10x/ess#272).
items.title: 0.50 — Aggregates over rows a when_related guard admits
items.summary: 0.50.0 is one synthesis fix: an aggregate view whose creating command has a when_related guard gets its aggregate scenario instead of being refused with ESS-SYNTH-017.
